beats.spoken: Every cosmetic pack in the EU has to show seven things.

That's Article 19 of the EU cosmetics regulation: indelible, easy to read and clearly visible. The first three are the name and address of the responsible person, the nominal content in grams or millilitres, and how long the product lasts.
Next come particular precautions for use, the batch number that identifies the product, and the function of the product, unless that's already clear from how it's presented.

The seventh is the list of ingredients, headed Ingredients. It can go on the outer packaging rather than the container itself. And packs under five grams or five millilitres don't need the content figure.

rows.text: may sit on the outer packaging
under 5 g or 5 ml: no content figure needed

beats.spoken: The US has its own rules. Federal law there also requires an ingredient list in descending order of predominance, and fragrance ingredients can be grouped as fragrance. Ingredients at one percent or less may follow in any order.
For you, that means: turn the pack over and go through all seven. If something important is missing, like the batch number or the address, it's fine to be sceptical.
Read the pack first, then apply. Beauty knowledge, clearly explained: follow Dewlane.
